LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a standard AUR package for the vector-view application, a GTK4 viewer for images, videos, PDFs, and office documents. The source fetches from the project's own GitHub tagged release (`https://github.com/Not-Bad-Company/vector/archive/refs/tags/v$pkgver.tar.gz`), which is the expected upstream source. The `prepare()` function runs `cargo fetch --locked` to retrieve Rust dependencies from crates.io, which is standard Rust packaging practice and not a supply-chain attack vector. The `build()` function uses `cargo build --frozen --release -p vector-view`, and `check()` runs `cargo test` — both normal Rust build/test operations. The `package()` function installs the built binary, desktop file, icon, license, and README to their respective system directories using standard `install` commands. There are no suspicious network downloads, obfuscated commands, eval/base64 usage, or any code that exfiltrates data, installs backdoors, or executes attacker-controlled content. All operations are consistent with ordinary AUR packaging practices for a Rust/Gtk application.
</details>
